basis: Marrow failure with hypogammaglobulinemia in 2/2; developmental disability in 2/2 and hypogonadism in 1/1. Pigmentation alone does not establish skin damage.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: hypogammaglobulinemia in 2/2 supports syndromic humoral immunodeficiency; the immune mechanism axis belongs in primary.

basis: The supplied definition establishes nerve-sheath origin; characteristic dermal or subcutaneous tumor location also establishes the skin axis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: this nerve-sheath tumor characteristically arises in the dermis or subcutis, so skin is a site of the tumor itself.

basis: Defining follicular skin tumors; pulmonary cysts and recurrent pneumothorax are frequent (30-79%). Renal carcinoma is a separately diagnosed predisposition outcome.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary cysts directly occupy lung tissue and cause pneumothorax; supplied frequencies are 30-79%, but they are not major diagnostic criteria.

basis: Defining renal tubular PTH resistance; cataracts and enamel hypoplasia each occur in 30-79% as syndromic manifestations. Skeletal damage is mostly below 30%.

decisions.renal: primary: the defining PTH resistance is localized renal tubular dysfunction; reduced renal hormone response is intrinsic functional impairment.
decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts are a direct hypocalcemic manifestation annotated in 30-79%, rather than merely a predisposition to an independent eye disease.

basis: Congenital encephalopathy with hypertonia and seizures. Respiratory failure in 2/2 does not establish direct damage to lung or airway tissue.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure is frequent (2/2) but reflects severe neurologic dysfunction; intrinsic lung or airway damage is not established.

basis: Muscular dystrophy, joint hyperlaxity and persistent keratotic skin changes define disease. Respiratory insufficiency in 4/4 is explicitly due to muscle weakness.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 4/4 is explicitly caused by skeletal muscle weakness; respiratory muscle disease belongs to musculoskeletal.

basis: Metabolic defect of bone and teeth mineralization; emphysema annotated 80-99% supports lung damage. Seizures (30-79%) omitted at cap; renal complications below 30%.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: supplied HPO explicitly annotates destructive emphysema in 80-99%; this supports lung involvement beyond chest deformity or respiratory symptoms.

basis: Severe neonatal hyperparathyroidism; fractures and renal tubular aminoaciduria each occur in 80-99%. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish functional injury.

decisions.renal: involved: aminoaciduria in 80-99% supports common intrinsic tubular reabsorptive dysfunction, beyond hypercalciuria or stone risk alone.

basis: Renal tubular dysgenesis commonly causes pulmonary hypoplasia through fetal anuria and deficient skull ossification through fetal hypotension; each occurs in >30%.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia is common (>30%) in the usual severe congenital course, arising from fetal anuria and oligohydramnios.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: deficient calvarial ossification is a characteristic common (>30%) developmental consequence of fetal renin-angiotensin dysfunction and hypotension.

basis: Mutilating keratoderma, deafness and digit loss define disease; cognitive impairment occurs in 30-79%. Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: cognitive impairment is annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting neurodevelopmental dysfunction; retained over hypogonadism at the cap.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (30-79%) qualifies, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of defining organs and cognitive impairment.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: mutilation with digit autoamputation is a defining feature, annotated in 80-99%; it directly destroys skeletal structures.
